scope: Bounded audit of complete original ICML predecessor workshop inventories for 1980 and 1985
policy: Bibliographic facts and source links only. PDFs inspected temporarily and removed; no PDFs hosted, authentication bypasses attempted, inferred paper titles added, or later book chapters silently relabeled as workshop papers.

1980.finding: No complete original workshop preprint inventory was recovered. The ICML 2006 proceedings preface explicitly distinguishes the 1980 workshop from a formal proceedings volume: a 1983 edited book was published instead. Contemporary author bibliographies nevertheless document workshop preprints. Therefore the gap concerns the complete original workshop inventory, not a verified missing formal proceedings volume.

relatedBook.title: Machine Learning: An Artificial Intelligence Approach
relatedBook.reasonNotImported: The publisher describes a collection of tutorials and research papers; Mostow's contemporary workshop report describes selected 1980 papers becoming the book. Its 16 chapters are not evidence of all original 1980 workshop preprints.

evidence.title: ICML 2006 proceedings preface, ANU repository copy
evidence.verification: Temporarily downloaded the 31-page repository file, extracted the preface, rendered PDF page 13 and visually confirmed the statement.
evidence.finding: The preface says a 1983 book was published instead of proceedings for the first workshop, and identifies 16 research papers in that book.

evidence.title: Jack Mostow, 1983 International Machine Learning Workshop: An Informal Report, July 18, 1983 draft
evidence.finding: Mostow describes the 1983 book as publishing selected papers from the 1980 workshop. The draft is explicitly an informal, non-exhaustive report.

evidence.title: Jaime Carbonell publications
evidence.finding: Lists Learning and Problem Solving by Analogy in Preprints of the CMU Machine Learning Workshop-Symposium, July 1980; supplies no complete workshop contents.

evidence.title: Machine Learning and Inference Laboratory publications
evidence.finding: Records several contributions to the Workshop on Current Developments in Machine Learning, July 16-18, 1980, but is a laboratory publication list rather than a complete event inventory.

1980.remainingRequirement: An organizer's complete preprint table of contents, original program with all contributed manuscripts, or equivalent archival inventory is required to enumerate the original workshop contributions.

event.name: Third International Workshop on Machine Learning

1985.finding: Original proceedings are supported by organizer correspondence and authors' own citations, but no complete public contents inventory was recovered. A specific DTIC accession was recovered through its OpenAlex catalogue record; the official public DTIC and NTIS endpoints returned HTTP 403. The later 77-paper book does not establish an exact original workshop inventory.

catalogueLead.title: Proceedings of the International Machine Learning Workshop (3rd) Held in Skytop, Pennsylvania on June 24-26, 1985.
catalogueLead.note: OpenAlex is a discovery aid. The underlying full document and its table of contents were not accessible, so the record does not verify either a complete inventory or whether the deposited document itself is the full proceedings rather than an accompanying report.
catalogueLead.accessResult: Both official endpoints returned HTTP 403; no access-control workaround attempted.
catalogueLead.archiveMirrorResult: Empty metadata object; no publicly catalogued item recovered at that identifier.

relatedBook.title: Machine Learning: A Guide to Current Research
relatedBook.reasonNotImported: The publisher says most contributions came from workshop participants; it does not assert that all chapters are workshop papers or that all original workshop papers are included. Authors document revisions between workshop papers and book chapters.

evidence.title: Tom M. Mitchell, workshop invitation dated April 4, 1985, Herbert A. Simon collection, CMU Libraries
evidence.verification: Temporarily downloaded and extracted the two-page original letter; PDF removed immediately after extraction.
evidence.finding: Confirms dates, Skytop venue, Rutgers host, organizing committee, and intended Kluwer proceedings; the invitation itself has no paper inventory.

evidence.title: Jack Mostow publications
evidence.finding: Lists the 1985 workshop paper Some requirements for effective replay of derivations on pages 129-132 and identifies the later book chapter Why are design derivations hard to replay? as a revised and condensed version. This directly establishes that book chapter metadata cannot be substituted mechanically for workshop metadata.

evidence.title: Raymond J. Mooney, Generalizing Explanations of Narratives into Schemata
evidence.finding: Verifies a 1985 workshop paper on pages 126-128, not a complete workshop inventory.

evidence.title: Machine Learning and Inference Laboratory publications
evidence.finding: Contains individual original 1985 proceedings citations and separately labels related book material as revised; does not expose a complete event contents list.

1985.remainingRequirement: A complete original proceedings table of contents or full organizer inventory, potentially from DTIC accession ADA175858 or Rutgers/organizer archives, is required before publishing an exact paper count or adding a complete 1985 inventory.

searchCoverage: ICML official historical conference list and ICML 2006 proceedings material
Organizer and author bibliographies at CMU, GMU, UT Austin and UNSW
CMU Libraries digitized original workshop correspondence
Springer publisher records for both related edited books
WorldCat bibliographic records for the edited books
OpenAlex discovery of the DTIC accession, followed by official DTIC and NTIS endpoint checks
Internet Archive public catalogue searches for workshop titles, Skytop, and machine-learning titles dated 1980-1986
Targeted Rutgers and CMU archival web searches; no complete contents inventory found
conclusion: Retain both original workshop inventories as unverified and do not count unknown inventories as zero papers. Refine the 1980 explanation to distinguish workshop preprints from formal proceedings. Do not substitute the 1983 16-chapter or 1986 77-paper edited books for exact workshop inventories.
